reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational structure of Spearman’s model rests on the assumption that performance variability stems from two distinct sources: a universal general factor (g) and domain-specific factors (s). The mathematical formulation treats performance P as a sum of weighted contributions from g, c, ω, o, and s. This implies a linear superposition principle where each component contributes additively to outcome variance. Dualities emerge in how g acts as both a global determinant and a residual in specific contexts. Failure modes occur when s dominates or when measurement error obscures true factor loadings. The model assumes static allocation of factors, yet real-world applications require dynamic adjustment. In GSI, this translates into probabilistic inference over latent variables; in GSE, it becomes a state-space representation of evolving cognitive profiles.
